entityDescription:
Headquartered in Espoo and founded on the Tammerkoski rapids in Tampere in 1865, Finland is one of Nokia’s most important locations.
Nokia in Finland is a community of around 6600 employees representing about 80 nationalities. There are three sites in Finland – Espoo, Tampere and Oulu. They play a key role in advanced technology development and in creating products and solutions for mobile networks as well as management systems.
Nokia employees help to evolve today’s networks, developing new products and conducting research into fields such as artificial intelligence, machine learning and autonomous transport.
Nokia works closely with universities, research institutes and other companies in Finland – building best-of-class technology to deliver collaborative advantage and enable impact at scale.
Finland hosts Nokia Technologies which focuses on our licensing business, covering patents, brand and technology. In addition, Finland is a key location forNokia Bell Labswith an unrivalled track record of innovation - 10 Nobel prizes. Nokia Finland is the clear leader in Nokia's patent applications globally: 25% of all Nokia's patent applications (first filings) in 2023 originated from Finland.

description:
Lechner Tudaskozpont Nonprofit Korlatolt Felelossegu Tarsasag (abbreviated official denomination in English: Lechner Non-profit Ltd.) was founded on January 24, 2013. Lechner Non-profit Ltd. is a professional background institution of the Prime Minister’s Office in the field of architecture, building and construction, real estate/land registration and geospatial issues. Its mission is to digitise and socialise wide range services connected to built environment and spatial data.

Its activities are focused on remote sensing, regional planning, smart city services as well as land surveying, earth observation and cartography tasks. Its services also include the operation of the Documentation Centre and IT services supported by e-administration.

Lechner Non-profit Ltd. acts as a mediator organisation between the architectural and co-professional fields and the wider public, its services reach both professional and residential users.

Since 2019 Lechner Non-profit Ltd. as background institution of the Prime Minister’s Office has become an organisation with the largest spatial data assets and the widest geospatial expertise. With transferring surveying, remote sensing and geospatial activities as well as land registration and cartography tasks from the former Office of the Capital City Budapest Department of Geodesy Remote Sensing and Land Offices (previously: Institute of Geodesy Cartography and Remote Sensing (FÖMI) to Lechner Non-profit Ltd., geospatial databases and resources are now concentrated in one single organisation.

#HorizonEurope

entityDescription:
SMHI, the Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute, is an expert Agency under the Ministry of the Environment and Energy. Through expertise in meteorology, hydrology, oceanography and climatology, SMHI contributes towards greater public welfare, increased safety and a sustainable society. SMHI administers and develops information about the weather, water and climate that provides social functions, trade and industry and the general public with knowledge and qualified decision guidance. National and international cooperation are extensive. SMHI offers tailored products and services that form the basis of important decision guidance for different activities. General forecasts and warnings, industryspecific services, simulations and analyses, statistics, climate studies and research assignments are just a few examples.
AGENCIES AND BUSINESS PARTNERS
SMHI’s activities are primarily financed in three ways: through grants, through commissions from other agencies and through business activities on commercial terms. There are distinct lines of activity that naturally are different, yet still based on the same fundamental principle, to contribute to greater public welfare, safety and a sustainable society. 
RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
SMHI conducts applied research in meteorology, hydrology, oceanography and climate. The research department develops knowledge, models and tools that describe processes in the atmosphere, in the sea and on land. These are needed to improve SMHI forecast models and decision guidance for practical public welfare. A great deal of the research conducted by SMHI is climate related. Researchers develop climate models, produce climate scenarios and participate in impact and adaptation studies. Mathematical models and methods that utilise data from satellites, radar systems and other observations are key in the research. SMHI’s research is mainly externally funded. Researchers collaborate in Swedish research projects, EU Projects and other international projects. 
CLIMATE WORK IN FOCUS
SMHI runs a national centre of knowledge for adaptation to climate change on behalf of the government at SMHI. The role of the centre is to act as a hub for knowledge about climate change and to be a meeting place for actors involved in climate change adaptation. SMHI is the contact point in Sweden for the UN’s climate panel, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). As the contact point, SMHI coordinates the Swedish IPCC work and establishes Contacts with the IPCC Secretariat in Geneva. Responsibility also entails nominating Swedish experts for the IPCC work. This can be in the role of author, reviewer or participating in workshops and other meetings.

entityDescription: QSENSATO s.r.l. aims to satisfy the growing market demand for sensors that are on the one hand robust, portable and miniaturized, on the other hand allowing ultra-precise and accurate measurements. Current atomic sensors lack such combined properties, due to the low versatility of the vapor cells used and the lack of integration with photonic structures. QSENSATO s.r.l. offers a solution based on an innovative fabrication method of laser-written vapor cells (LWVCs) with 3D versatility and unique integration with photonic waveguides and optical fibres. The company is developing and will commercialize the following products: 1. LWVCs tailored for different sensing and metrology applications. 2. atomic-photonic chips, i.e. LWVCs integrated with photonic structures. 3. complete quantum sensors such as optically pumped magnetometers, electric field sensors, frequency references, atomic clocks and gyroscopes. QSENSATO s.r.l. activities will also be devoted to research and development of technologies related to the main one.

entityDescription:
Menapia Ltd was established in 2020 with the goal of advancing atmospheric data collection through automated, high-altitude Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS). Our flagship service, the MetSprite platform, provides "Atmospheric Profiling as a Service," delivering continuous, high-resolution atmospheric data to our clients.
With MetSprite, we offer hourly atmospheric profiles up to 2 km altitude, measuring calibrated temperature, relative humidity, and two-dimensional wind data. We also provide extended profiling up to 6 km and the option to integrate custom sensors, ensuring tailored solutions for a wide range of applications.
Our mission is to create a comprehensive atmospheric monitoring system that enhances weather and climate forecasting capabilities. Led by a team of experts in aerospace, physics, and meteorology—including our CEO John Mooney, Chief Aerospace Officer Peter Mooney, and Chief Meteorological Officer Ben Pickering—we are committed to advancing atmospheric science and operational meteorology.

entityName: University of Alexander Dubcek in Trencin
entityDescription:
University of Alexander Dubcek In Trencin (TnUAD) is a modern university in Slovakia, focusing on applied research and education in engineering, materials science, and technology. The university has robust capabilities in the development of advanced materials, surface engineering, and testing of innovative solutions, particularly in metallic and composite materials. Its research infrastructure includes state-of-the-art laboratories for material analysis, nanotechnology, and 3D printing, supporting applications in aerospace and space technologies.
TnUAD is actively engaged in international collaborations and interdisciplinary research aimed at innovation in lightweight materials, high-strength alloys, and thermal-resistant coatings. The university also offers expertise in computational modeling, structural optimization, and advanced manufacturing processes. With its focus on applied research and industry partnerships, TnUAD is well-positioned to contribute to the advancement of space technology and related fields.

The university comprises several key faculties and research units:

- Faculty of Industrial Technologies: Specializes in materials science, nanotechnology, and advanced manufacturing processes, with significant applications in aerospace and space technologies.

- Faculty of Special Technology: Focuses on robotics, mechatronics, and special-purpose machinery, providing high-precision solutions for technical challenges in various industries.

- Faculty of Social and Economic Relations: Supports interdisciplinary projects with economic and managerial expertise, fostering collaboration across sectors.

- Faculty of Health Care: Conducts research in medical technologies, complementing the university's engineering and technical research focus.

entityName: University of Maribor, Faculty of Law
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Law at The University of Maribor represents an important part of Legal education in Slovenia and helps in developing not only the field of Higher education but also all other aspects of Slovenian society that the law is an integral part of. The law education in The Faculty of Law at The University of Maribor, is widely interconnected with the Slovenian judiciary, lawyers and prosecutors. Our graduates are highly valued when working in the State Administration and Local Government Bodies and mostly when working as lawyers in companies and financial institutions.

The development of The Faculty of Law at the University of Maribor deriving from the College of Law (in 1960-1990) and from the High School of Law (in 1990-1993) is a result of plenty years of effort of all employees, professors, assistants, researchers and other associates working towards a better Faculty and better study environment for its students. Law is one of the first fields ever to be studied by humans being, also, of major importance to other fields of study, especially those connected to social sciences, as all knowledge about society is somehow connected its order. Law is much more than a system of rules, it is a philosophy that expresses a unique overview of the world and all the people in it. By determining the basic Human Rights and freedoms, law contributes to the creation of a better society. Law is also sociology, in the way its regulation of social encounters sheds a light on them and on their nature – whether wanted, normal, good or bad, allowed or forbidden. Furthermore, law is also a strategy and a helpful instrument in changing the society.

entityName: University of Maribor, Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at the University of Maribor is one of the leading teaching and research institutions in the field of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science in Slovenia. Faculty provides students with knowledge based on internationally recognized scientific research work, thus enabling them to be successfully integrated within future working environments in Slovenia and/or abroad. We aim to strengthen the positions of our internationally-recognized university education and research institutions within the fields of electrical engineering, computer science, information technology, communications, media, telecommunications, and mechatronics, throughout Central Europe. Research assumes a vital place in the activities of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science. An important element in the current, quality pedagogical work is following the latest events in the world and being creative and cooperative in the development of our own scientific research work.

Our slogan is "Create your future through knowledge and teamwork". At the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at the University of Maribor we create knowledge based on the results of internationally recognized scientific research work, and we pass it on to students and society, thus enabling them to address challenges in working environments successfully, both in Slovenia and abroad. Our vision is to consolidate the position of an internationally-recognized university educational and research institution within the fields of Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Media Communications, Telecommunications and Mechatronics, throughout Central Europe, which is high quality and attractive to students, and addresses the challenges of society and the economy in Slovenia and abroad.

entityName: University of Maribor, Faculty of Agriculture and Life Sciences
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Agriculture and Life Sciences at The University of Maribor mission is research, education and knowledge transfer to meet the needs of agriculture, food processing and related industries and co-creation of public opinion and active policy in favour of food security, self-sufficiency in natural, environmentally friendly and locally produced food, preservation of cultivated agricultural land, increasing biodiversity, reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and other pollutants in the environment. Our values are based on honesty, curiosity, creativity, freedom of spirit, cooperation and knowledge exchange, care for people and sustainable development, enriching agricultural knowledge, raising awareness, strengthening humanistic values, creating dialogue, increasing quality of life and global justice. Our slogan is "Knowledge and Tradition".

We strive to produce internationally recognized research, to be an educational and innovative centre for agriculture, food and renewable resources. We create new cutting-edge fundamental and applied knowledge, which is passed on to national and international researchers and graduates, as well as to farms and businesses. Furthermore, we work on identifying the problems and challenges of the 21st century and on finding solutions through responsive research. We also try to redesign our study programmes in a way that we believe is fit for the future. Another aim is to be centre with intensive international exchange of professors, researchers and students, a development incubator and a space for demonstrations of innovation and analysis and an important stakeholder in agricultural, food, economic and environmental policymaking.

entityName: University of Maribor, Faculty of Medicine
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Medicine at the University of Maribor is an educational and research institution at which we educate students to acquire knowledge and skills needed for prevention of diseases, maintenance and recovery of health; an institution where we, within institutes, implement research work and where we are, besides this, concerned with integrated and sustainable development of an individual and social responsibility.

Our vision is to be a respectable, desirable, established, safe, internationally oriented and recognizable educational and research institution with the elements of excellence and to be a part of close and distant environment, known for knowledge and competency of physicians whom it had educated, professors, researchers and technical staff who work in it and known for moral standards which adorn it. We are concerned with consistent development of all chairs and institutes and also with the development of our clinical teaching bases. With intensive international exchanges of students and professors we facilitate, for students and professors, acquiring of additional knowledge and experiences. An important task for the future is intensification of research work, especially basic research, which we achieve in cooperation with other faculties at the University of Maribor which have already now been included as partners at the postgraduate study programme Biomedical technology, in cooperation with the University Clinical Centre Maribor and in cooperation with our partner faculties within the European Union. The Faculty of Medicine at the University of Maribor endeavour to continually renew study programmes in the sense of modernization, while cooperating with students and taking into consideration guidelines which are formed by international organizations such as AMSE (Association of Medical Schools in Europe) and AMEE (Association for Medical Education in Europe). For this purpose, a curriculum committee has been established which is responsible for constant modernization of curricula.

The basic task of the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Maribor as an educational institution of future physicians is education of our graduate in the technical sense and also in the sense of ethical norms. Competencies which must be mastered by our graduates are in congruence with competencies encompassed in the national Blue Book on education of physicians and also with the standards of our partner European faculties.
